title: Citrine Banking inference cost rewrite proposal
content:
Summary:

This note summarizes a before/after cost model for Citrine Banking's API usage and a proposed set of Redwood Optimize changes (prefix KV caching, batching adjustments, quantization profile, and a fallback routing policy) to achieve lower monthly inference spend while meeting the customer's p95 latency SLO of 250ms for standard chat flows. This is a working proposal for SE->customer review; numbers are from our pilot logs (Aug–Sep 2025) and internal unit-cost models.

Customer context:
- Customer: Citrine Banking (digital-first retail bank; 3rd-party partner integration)
- Current deployment: Hosted Redwood API using medium-large open-chat model (r/w mixture) with 8k context, running in us-east-1, no KV cache enabled, standard batching (max_batch_size=8), default FP16 runtime.
- Monthly traffic: ~150M input tokens + 300M output tokens (total 450M tokens) typical; 95th percentile peak 2.4x baseline.
- SLA: p95 < 250ms for interactive workflows; background batch jobs allowed higher latency.

Baseline (current) cost model — monthly (observed):
- Tokens: 450,000,000 tokens
- Model runtime unit cost (hosted internal): $0.00008 per token = $36,000
- Networking/storage misc: $1,200
- Embedding/rerank jobs (periodic): $4,800
- Total baseline monthly inference-related spend: $42,000
- Observed latency (p50/p95): 95ms / 230ms
- Notes: High cold token overhead for repeated customer prompts where prefix is common; no KV caching means repeated prefix computation costs.

Redwood Optimize recommendations (summary):
1) Prefix KV caching (session-level 60% hit target) — store shared prompts and few-shot context for common flows.
2) Adjust batching policy (increase max_batch_size to 16 for background and non-interactive calls, keep 8 for interactive with adaptive short-window batching).
3) Quantization: deploy INT8 quant profile with mixed-fp16 fallbacks on long sequences (expected quality delta <1.5% on our eval set).
4) Model variant routing: primary -> quantized variant; fallback to full-precision variant on NLU confidence < 0.6.
5) Autoscaling tweak: enable burst-capacity floor to drop 10% of p95 latency during peak.

Projected after-optimization (monthly) — three scenarios: conservative / expected / aggressive
- Assumptions common to all scenarios: baseline traffic unchanged; embedding jobs unchanged.

1) Conservative (KV hit 30%, quant savings 15%, batching benefit 5%):
  - Effective token compute-equivalent: baseline * (1 - 0.30)* (1 - 0.15)* (1 - 0.05) = ~0.571 of baseline tokens => ~257M tokens equivalent
  - Model runtime cost: $20,560
  - Networking/storage: $1,200
  - Embedding jobs: $4,800
  - Total monthly: $26,560 => ~36.7% savings vs baseline
  - Latency (p50/p95): 110ms / 240ms (small increase at p50 due to batching changes, p95 roughly same)

2) Expected (KV hit 50%, quant savings 25%, batching benefit 12%):
  - Compute-equivalent: baseline * 0.5 * 0.75 * 0.88 = ~0.33 => ~148M tokens equivalent
  - Model runtime cost: $11,840
  - Networking/storage: $1,200
  - Embedding jobs: $4,800
  - Total monthly: $17,840 => ~57.5% savings vs baseline
  - Latency (p50/p95): 100ms / 200ms (p95 improves due to cache hits on common flows)

3) Aggressive (KV hit 65%, quant savings 35%, batching benefit 18%):
  - Compute-equivalent: baseline * 0.35 * 0.65 * 0.82 = ~0.186 => ~84M tokens equivalent
  - Model runtime cost: $6,720
  - Networking/storage: $1,200
  - Embedding jobs: $4,800
  - Total monthly: $12,720 => ~69.7% savings vs baseline
  - Latency (p50/p95): 85ms / 180ms (improved for cached flows, non-cached flows may still see no change)

Quick sensitivity table (monthly model runtime cost only):
- KV hit 0% / 30% / 50% / 65% (with expected quant 25% & batching 12%):
  - 0% hit => tokens 450M * (1 - 0)*(1 - 0.25)*(1 - 0.12) = 450M * 0.66 = 297M => $23,760
  - 30% hit => tokens 297M * (1 - 0.30) = 208M => $16,640
  - 50% hit => tokens ~148M => $11,840 (same as expected scenario)
  - 65% hit => tokens ~104M => $8,320

Implementation checklist (high level):
- [ ] Pilot KV cache for the two most common flows (login-help, balance-inquiry) with 2-week A/B sampling
- [ ] Create quantized model variant and run automated evals & human eval for quality regression (target delta <2%)
- [ ] Update routing policy in pilot region and configure fallback thresholds (confidence, error rate)
- [ ] Load test with synthetic peak (2.5x) and measure p95 impact; adjust burst-capacity floor if p95 > 250ms
- [ ] Prepare rollout runbook: metrics dashboard (cost per million tokens, cache hit %, p95 latency, fallback rate) + runbook for rollback

Risks & mitigations:
- Quality regression (risk): small hallucination/regression on long-context financial QAs. Mitigation: gated rollout, human eval, canary on 5% traffic.
- Cache staleness (risk): user-specific prefixes may leak or become stale. Mitigation: strict TTLs, session scoping, encryption-in-transit, audit logs.
- Hidden traffic patterns (risk): rare large documents causing long sequences that reduce quant benefits. Mitigation: routing large-sequence jobs to full-precision pool.

Open questions for Citrine SE/Infra:
- Acceptable canary size for customer? (we suggested 5–10%)
- Are there any regulatory constraints preventing session-level KV caching for PII-bearing prompts?
- Required lead time for their security review for quantized model artifacts (HSM/KMS signing)?

Next steps (owner: Maya Chen):
- Share this note with Citrine SEs and Solutions Eng to confirm flows and dataset for KV cache (by 2025-11-07).
- Create a small demo runbook + dashboards and propose a 30-day pilot window.
- If customer signs pilot, spin up the quantized variant branch and open OPT-321 for rollout tracking.

Appendix: example micro-simulation (quick):
- Baseline per-request: avg input 30 tokens, avg output 60 tokens, prefix repeated 40 tokens each time across 70% of sessions.
- With KV cache (50% hit) we avoid recomputing the 40-token prefix on half of sessions -> direct token compute reduction = 40 tokens * 0.5 * total_sessions (~1.5M sessions/month) => ~30M tokens saved at compute layer.

Notes to self / rough action items (short):
- Ask infra for exact per-token unit cost for INT8 variant (we used conservative 25% savings assumption).
- Get sample of 10k sessions to compute real prefix repetition distribution.
- Schedule 30-min sync with Citrine SE next week to align pilot metrics.

End of draft.
